watch_reasons.upstream-dep-a: Watched because this library is an upstream dependency of a project the operator maintains. Only genuinely actionable items -- breaking changes, deprecations, new capabilities worth adopting -- matter here. A generic marketing page, a bare list of past release dates with no specifics, or legal/licensing terms are NOT actionable, even though the library itself is relevant.
watch_reasons.upstream-dep-b: Watched because this service is an upstream dependency of the operator's own stack. Only genuinely actionable items -- breaking changes, deprecations, new capabilities worth adopting -- matter here. General API reference documentation the operator could look up any time they actually need it is NOT actionable on its own.
watch_reasons.upstream-dep-c: Watched because this SDK is an upstream dependency of the operator's own stack. Only genuinely actionable items -- breaking changes, deprecations, new capabilities worth adopting -- matter here. Generic how-to documentation the operator could look up any time they actually need it is NOT actionable on its own, even if well-written and legitimate.
watch_reasons.upstream-dep-d: Watched because this platform is an upstream dependency of the operator's own stack. Only genuinely actionable items -- breaking changes, deprecations, new capabilities worth adopting -- matter here.
watch_reasons.vendor-announcements: Watched for general awareness of official model/agent-ecosystem announcements (new models, API changes, deprecations) from major AI vendors. A wider bar than the upstream-dep-* topics -- a major official announcement from a frontier lab is relevant even without an immediate action item, since it shapes the operator's overall strategy.
watch_reasons.ecosystem-awareness: Watched for major releases in the agent-framework and protocol-SDK ecosystem generally. This is ecosystem awareness, not a tracked dependency -- a well-known, actively maintained project or SDK release is NOT automatically high-value just for being legitimate and popular. It should only score high if it represents a genuinely major shift (e.g. a breaking protocol version change) as opposed to routine incremental development.
watch_reasons.conference-activity: Watched for research-conference activity (deadlines, accepted papers, agenda highlights) at top venues. Routine conference-logistics pages (submission portals, call-for-papers boilerplate, generic navigation hubs) are NOT actionable -- only genuinely notable content (a highlighted paper, a deadline change, a notable trend) is.

cases.title: How Claude's text watermarking works
cases.content: Explains Anthropic's text watermarking in Claude to comply with the EU AI Act. Works by subtly altering the source of randomness when Claude selects among equally viable word choices, creating an undetectable pattern verifiable with a special key. No quality impact, no added cost/latency. Based on Google DeepMind's SynthID-Text method; less effective on factual/heavily-edited content where word choices are limited.

cases.title: RFC: deprecate built-in replay console log capture
cases.content: GitHub RFC issue proposing to deprecate PostHog's built-in console log capture in session replay in favor of the dedicated logs product. Currently two capture paths exist (legacy log_entries table vs newer logs product); proposal is a four-phase migration to remove the legacy path.

cases.title: The 2026-07-28 Specification
cases.content: MCP released version 2026-07-28, a fundamental shift from stateful bidirectional protocol to stateless request/response. Removes session handshakes, adds Multi Round-Trip Requests, header-based routing, cacheable list responses, RFC 9207 auth compliance, formal extensions support. All four Tier-1 SDKs (TypeScript/Python/Go/C#) updated; 12-month deprecation window for legacy features.
